in_sanskrit.name: शैला
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Feminine form of शैल (Shaila), which means mountain, hill, peak, or rock. This name is derived from the Sanskrit root शिल (shila), meaning 'rock'.

in_hindi.name: शैला
in_hindi.long_meaning: Shaila is a Hindi name that is derived from the Sanskrit word शैल (shaila), meaning mountain, hill, peak, or rock. In Hindi, the name is written as शैला (Shaila) and is formed by combining the words गिरि (giri), meaning mountain, and ला (la), a suffix that is used to form feminine names.

in_tamil.name: சாயலா
in_tamil.long_meaning: Shaila is a Tamil name that is derived from the Sanskrit word शैल (shaila), meaning mountain or hill. In Tamil, the name is written as சாயலா (Cayala) and is pronounced as 'Saya-la'.

in_telugu.name: శైలా
in_telugu.long_meaning: Shaila is a Telugu name that is derived from the Sanskrit word शैल (shaila), meaning mountain, hill, peak, or rock. In Telugu, the name is written as శైలా (Shaila) and is formed by combining the words గిరి (giri), meaning mountain, and ఆ (aa), a suffix that is used to form feminine names.

vedic_reference.note: Shaila is a Vedic name that is mentioned in various Hindu texts and mythologies. In the Mahabharata, there is a character named Shaila, who is a Rakshasa (demon) and the father of the monkey king Hanuman. In the Puranas, Shaila is also mentioned as a mountain peak in the Himalayas and a river in Kashmir.
